definitions.explanation: A Shinto ritual performed by a priest to cleanse people, places, or objects of impurities, evil spirits, or bad luck. Commonly performed at shrines for various occasions.

examples.japanese: {神社|じんじゃ}でお{祓|はら}いを{受|う}けた。
examples.english: I received a purification ritual at the shrine.

examples.japanese: {新車|しんしゃ}を{買|か}ったので、お{祓|はら}いをしてもらった。
examples.english: I bought a new car, so I had a purification ritual performed on it.

examples.japanese: {厄年|やくどし}なので、{年|ねん}の{初|はじ}めに{厄除|やくよ}けのお{祓|はら}いに{行|い}ってきた。
examples.english: Since it's my unlucky year, I went for an evil-warding purification at the start of the year.

notes:
CULTURE:
お{祓|はら}い is one of the most common Shinto rituals in Japan. People seek purification for a wide range of occasions: moving into a new house, buying a new car, starting a business, reaching an unlucky year ({厄年|やくどし}), or after a period of misfortune.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{祓|はら}いを{受|う}ける (to receive a purification)
- お{祓|はら}いをしてもらう (to have a purification performed)
- お{祓|はら}いに{行|い}く (to go for a purification)

FORM:
The お prefix is standard and almost always used. The plain form {祓|はら}い exists but is less common in everyday speech.
